title: AML Detective: Singapore KYC Files
intro: You are Detective Riley, assigned by the Head Detective to investigate AML/KYC alerts that may involve laundering networks.
disclaimer: This game is educational and set in a fictionalized Singapore regulatory context. It is not legal advice and should not be treated as universal regulation.

cases.title: The Marina Trading Mystery
cases.opening: Head Detective: A transaction-monitoring alert flagged repeated cash deposits followed by overseas transfers from Marina Trading Pte. Ltd.

evidence.description: KYC profile lists low expected turnover but account activity spikes 6x in 2 weeks.
Twelve deposits just below reporting threshold across multiple branches.
Customer explanation conflicts with invoice dates and values.
A legitimate seasonal payment to a known domestic vendor.

actions.narrative: You find a mismatch between declared activity and actual turnover.

actions.text: Review transactions and follow transaction chains
actions.narrative: Structured deposits and linked international transfers appear in a repeating pattern.

actions.text: Interview the customer and request additional documentation
actions.narrative: The customer provides inconsistent explanations and incomplete support documents.

conclusions.label: Escalate for suspicious activity review and enhanced due diligence
Mark as false positive and close alert
Restrict account immediately without escalation rationale

cases.actual_activity: A likely layering pattern through a shell counterparty using structured deposits and rapid outward transfers.
cases.recommended_approach: Aggregate linked transactions, verify source of funds, and escalate through formal suspicious activity workflow.

cases.title: Nominee Director Network
cases.opening: Head Detective: An import/export client recently onboarded in Singapore routes funds to entities in two high-risk jurisdictions with unclear ownership.

evidence.description: Corporate registry extracts show nominee director overlap across three shell-like entities.
Payment chain includes round-dollar invoices and immediate pass-through transfers.
One high-value transfer maps to legitimate commodity settlement terms.
Beneficial owner declaration omits controlling party linked through trust structure.

actions.narrative: Cross-entity registry checks reveal repeating nominee structures.

actions.text: Investigate beneficial owners and escalate customer for enhanced due diligence
actions.narrative: Enhanced due diligence reveals hidden control through a trust nominee chain.

actions.text: Follow transaction chains and compare stated business with actual flows
actions.narrative: You separate one legitimate payment from a broader circular layering pattern.

conclusions.label: Escalate for suspicious activity and recommend temporary transaction restrictions
Clear customer as fully legitimate based on one valid invoice
Accuse nominee director as sole actor without ownership analysis

cases.actual_activity: A mixed-flow account used both for legitimate trade payments and for layered movements routed through nominee-controlled entities.
key_red_flags: Use of shell entities in high-risk corridors
cases.recommended_approach: Combine beneficial ownership verification with chain analysis before deciding escalation and account controls.

cases.title: Correspondent Maze
cases.opening: Head Detective: A correspondent banking client may be moving fraud proceeds through nested accounts, crypto off-ramps, and trade invoices.

evidence.description: Adverse media links a controlling shareholder to prior mule account investigations.
Nested transfers fan out to newly opened personal accounts before crypto conversion.
Source-of-wealth file contains unsupported declarations and recycled audit letters.
One seemingly suspicious transfer is tied to a genuine emergency supplier payment.

actions.text: Review sanctions/PEP/adverse-media information and internal intelligence
actions.narrative: You identify historical indicators linking controllers to mule-account operations.

actions.text: Trace overseas payment chains through correspondent and crypto off-ramps
actions.narrative: Layering routes emerge, but one transfer has a legitimate emergency rationale.

actions.text: Examine source of funds and source of wealth evidence for controlling parties
actions.narrative: Declared wealth documentation appears recycled and unsupported by independent records.

conclusions.label: Escalate suspicious activity and recommend coordinated correspondent controls
Conclude all transactions are legitimate due to mixed evidence
Freeze all related accounts immediately without proportional analysis

cases.actual_activity: Fraud proceeds are layered through nested correspondent accounts and partially blended with legitimate payments to reduce detection confidence.
cases.recommended_approach: Use risk-based proportional controls: validate source evidence, isolate legitimate flows, and escalate suspicious patterns with documented rationale.
